greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who cleanses the temple of our hearts, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the Word of God made flesh. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you drive out the darkness from our souls. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you promise a sweetness that never fades. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: How sweet to my taste is your promise!
homily:
Imagine for a moment the sensation of something small, something you hold in your hand that carries a weight far greater than its size. In the book of Revelation, John is given a scroll. It is a small scroll, easily held, yet it contains the very words of heaven. He is told to take it and swallow it. It is a strange, visceral image. He is told that in his mouth, it will taste as sweet as honey, but in his stomach, it will turn sour. There is a profound honesty in this. The word of God is a delight to the palate—it is the truth we crave, the promise we cling to, the honey that sustains us when the world is bitter. But to digest it, to let it become part of our very life, is a different matter. It requires us to hold both the sweetness of the promise and the sourness of the struggle, to let the light of God work its way into the deepest, most aching parts of our human experience. 

I want you to hold onto this image: the scroll. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he interacted with the world. He was a boy who loved the mechanics of things, a boy who built games and applications, who coded, who understood that behind every interface, there is a logic, a structure, a purpose. Benjamin was a boy who looked at the world with a brilliant, searching mind, always seeking to understand how the systems of life fit together. He was a boy who found joy in the small, technical details, whether it was the flight paths of the airplanes he loved or the logic of a new piece of software. He lived with an openness that was like an open scroll, ready to receive, ready to learn, ready to be filled with the truth. And yet, we know that the scroll of life is not always easy to swallow. We know that the sweetness of his presence, the way he would wake up every morning to say, 'Good morning, Dad,' the way he would share his dreams of 'con chim airlines' with a giggle—these are memories that are honey to your souls. But the reality of his absence, the five months that have passed since he went home to God, is the sourness that sits in the stomach. It is the ache that does not leave. It is the reality that life, for all its beauty, is also a place of profound, undeniable mystery.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who carry the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: the house is quiet. The routines have changed. There are moments when the silence is so loud it feels like it might break you. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden, sharp ambush of sorrow in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go. 

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus enters the temple. He sees that it has been turned into a den of thieves. He cleanses it. He restores it to its true purpose: a house of prayer. This is the hinge of the mystery. We often think that God is hidden, that he is behind the sealed scroll, that he is waiting in some distant heaven. But Jesus shows us that God is the one who walks the streets with us. He is the one who enters the temple of our lives to clear out the noise, the grief, the confusion, and the fear, so that we might find a space for prayer. When we feel overwhelmed, when the scroll of our lives feels too bitter to swallow, Jesus is there to remind us that he is the one who has already tasted the bitterness of the cross. He has been there. He has entered the depths of human sorrow and come out the other side. He is the one who makes our hearts a house of prayer again. Benjamin, in his own way, understood this. He was a boy who was willing to offer his own 'piggy bank'—his own security—for the sake of his uncle. He was a boy who understood that love is not about keeping; it is about giving. That is the logic of the Kingdom. That is the code that truly matters.

Consider the sweetness of the promise. The Psalm tells us, 'How sweet to my taste is your promise!' This is the turn of the heart. The blessing of the Lord is not that we will never suffer, but that we will never be abandoned in our suffering. Benjamin is now resting in that promise. He is dwelling in the land of the living, fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven, standing alongside kindred spirits, watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where you and Ben were standing outside room 419, and he said with that earnest, familiar voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the shared laughter, the way you both navigated the world together. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lord who cleansed the temple is the Lord who cleanses your hearts of despair, leaving behind only the sweetness of his presence.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the peace of heaven, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus. Go in peace.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace.
For all who are grieving today, that God may console their hearts, strengthen their spirits, and fill them with the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, heard a voice from heaven speak to me.
Then the voice spoke to me and said:
“Go, take the scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel
who is standing on the sea and on the land.”
So I went up to the angel and told him to give me the small scroll.
He said to me, “Take and swallow it.
It will turn your stomach sour,
but in your mouth it will taste as sweet as honey.”
I took the small scroll from the angel’s hand and swallowed it.
In my mouth it was like sweet honey,
but when I had eaten it, my stomach turned sour.
Then someone said to me, “You must prophesy again
about many peoples, nations, tongues, and kings.”

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (103a) How sweet to my taste is your promise!
In the way of your decrees I rejoice,
as much as in all riches.
R. How sweet to my taste is your promise!
Yes, your decrees are my delight;
 they are my counselors.
R. How sweet to my taste is your promise!
The law of your mouth is to me more precious
than thousands of gold and silver pieces.
R. How sweet to my taste is your promise!
How sweet to my palate are your promises,
sweeter than honey to my mouth!
R. How sweet to my taste is your promise!
Your decrees are my inheritance forever;
the joy of my heart they are.
R. How sweet to my taste is your promise!
I gasp with open mouth
in my yearning for your commands.
R. How sweet to my taste is your promise!

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus entered the temple area and proceeded to drive out
those who were selling things, saying to them,
“It is written,
My house shall be a house of prayer,
but you have made it a den of thieves.”
And every day he was teaching in the temple area.
The chief priests, the scribes, and the leaders of the people, meanwhile,
were seeking to put him to death,
but they could find no way to accomplish their purpose
because all the people were hanging on his words.

pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
